name: correlation-not-null-column
summary: A migration widens users with a NOT NULL tenant_id column, and the struct that writes the row gains a plain string field in the same commit. Each half is unremarkable. Together they say every insert that does not set TenantID writes an empty string into a column the schema was just made to require, and the migration itself fails outright if the table has rows.
why_this_fixture_exists: This is the case that justifies a second wave at all. The migration pane sees SQL and no Go. A Go provider sees a new struct field and no SQL. Neither can reach the conclusion, and an LLM given both can.

expect.what: The new NOT NULL column and the new non-pointer struct field are about the same data, and nothing fills the column for rows that already exist or for inserts that omit the field.

quiet.about: restating the migration finding on its own
quiet.note: The NOT NULL column with no default is already a wave-one finding. Saying it again is not a review.
